failures.criterion: A2 T2: a leased loop's tick is counted in the period it was due in, so a lone process never loses a period (PR body Change line 1)
failures.evidence: duty.Exclusive measures time.Since(due) in the process (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/duty/exclusive.go:230) and the database subtracts it from its own now(), read when the statement starts; any stall between the two (a descheduled or GC-paused process, a slow socket write) moves the tick's boundary later by the stall, so a tick due within that stall of a boundary still lands in the next period and the on-time tick after it is refused: the INFRA-523 defect, narrowed from the lease acquire to one send but not removed. Red test committed: packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/duty/exclusive_latency_test.go, TestExclusiveCountsATickStalledAfterItsMeasureInThePeriodItWasDueIn (every write on the lease connection stalls 100 ms during the first tick, due 50 ms before a boundary; same shape as TestExclusiveCountsALateTickInThePeriodItWasDueIn's 400 ms acquire delay). Command: cd packages/envoy && go test -count=3 -v -run '^TestExclusiveCountsATickStalledAfterItsMeasureInThePeriodItWasDueIn$' ./internal/dispatch/duty/ -> FAIL 3/3 'exclusive_latency_test.go:73: the tick due one period after a stalled one was refused (first due 50ms before a boundary, its writes stalled 100ms each); a lone loop lost that period'. Control: the same test with the stall set to 0 passes 3/3, so the failure is the stall. Every other TestExclusive* passes.
